meta.name: spam_detection
meta.title: Spam detection
meta.description: Realistic emails labelled for whether they are unwanted spam and whether they are phishing that impersonates a trusted party.

is_spam.instructions: Is `email` unwanted mail the recipient never asked for, such as bulk advertising, a scam or a phishing attempt?

is_phishing.instructions: Does `email` impersonate a trusted party to get the recipient to hand over passwords, payment details or personal data, or to open a malicious link or attachment?

tags.legit_personal: Legitimate personal email from friends or family.
tags.legit_work: Legitimate workplace email from colleagues, managers, clients or internal teams.
tags.legit_transactional: Legitimate receipts, confirmations, bills or shipping notices for something the recipient did.
tags.legit_security_alert: Genuine security notice from the real service domain, with no credential request.
tags.legit_newsletter: Marketing or newsletter mail the recipient clearly opted into (account reference, unsubscribe).
tags.spam_promo: Unsolicited bulk advertising for products or services.
tags.spam_seo: Unsolicited SEO, link-building, lead-list or agency marketing pitches.
tags.spam_crypto: Unsolicited crypto, investment or get-rich-quick schemes.
tags.spam_prize: Fake prizes, lotteries or 'you've been selected' offers.
tags.spam_scam: Advance-fee, romance or job scams that don't impersonate a party the recipient trusts.
tags.spam_obfuscated: Spam using obfuscated spelling (V1agra, spaced letters) to evade filters.
tags.spam_image: Image-only or 'see attached flyer' advertising with little text.
tags.phishing_credential: Impersonates a trusted service to harvest login or card credentials.
tags.phishing_invoice: Fake invoice, receipt, payment-change or malicious document attachment.
tags.phishing_bec: Business email compromise: impersonates a colleague or executive to get gift cards, wires or payroll changes.
tags.phishing_delivery: Fake courier or postal notice asking for a fee or personal details.
tags.phishing_tax: Fake tax-authority refund asking for bank, card or identity details.
tags.phishing_it: Fake IT helpdesk asking for passwords, MFA codes or re-registration.
tags.easy: A shallow keyword reader would get this right.
tags.hard: A careful reader gets it right, but surface cues (urgency, salesy tone, polish) point the wrong way.

input.email:
From: Hearthside Recipes <privacy@hearthsiderecipes.com>
To: Tara Quinn <tara.quinn@postbox.example>
Subject: Important information about your account security

Dear Tara,
On October 3 we discovered that an outside party accessed a database containing usernames and hashed passwords for some Hearthside accounts, including yours.
Payment information is stored separately and was not affected.
As a precaution, we've signed you out everywhere. Next time you open Hearthside you'll be asked to create a new password.
We're sorry. Full details are on our blog at hearthsiderecipes.com/security.

rationale: A data-breach disclosure from a service the user has an account with explains what happened and recommends changing the password in the app, without a login link or credential request.

From: Remittance Advice <remit@payments-advice.example>
